name: Bekwil
world_status: statement found in an open source
sweep_summary: Bekwil (bekw1242) is not in the catalog. Of the two title-sweep items, one is noise: Wells & Corrin 2004 (children's turn-taking, TSL 62) is linked to Bekwil only by Glottolog's automated keyword assignment from 'overlap' (stated on Glottolog ref 510411); nothing to acquire. The other, Bouka 1995 (ULB PhD, 386 pp., 'Structures phonologiques et structures prosodiques: le modèle bekwel'), is the only extended description of Bekwel (Congo) and the best candidate for a stress/prosody statement, but no digital copy exists anywhere checked (Glottolog, HAL, CORE, Crossref, BnF, Google Books, ULB DI-fusion unusable, not held by the libraries we checked): library-print-only, priority high (ILL from ULB). Cheucle 2014's second-hand citations of it (pp. 47-95 diphthongs, 238-251 syllable/coda, tonal data) suggest its 'prosodic structures' are syllable structure and tone. Best first-hand statement actually read: Cheucle 2014 (Lyon 2 thesis, already on file under koon1245, pp. 1-169 recovered; live Lyon 2 server timed out, HAL deposit is metadata-only, Internet Archive offline today), Bekwel phonology sketch pp. 159-161: two tonemes /H/, /B/ (registers H, B, M; patterns H, B, HB, BH), tone lexical and grammatical; the sketch and its recapitulative table never mention stress or accent (zero hits for accent/stress/prosod in 169 pp.), so the language reads as tonal and silent on word stress. Files and Other Glottolog Bekwil refs not in the title sweep but relevant for a future fetch: Avore 2002 'Description phonologique du Bakwel de Makokou' (Univ. Omar Bongo mémoire, no copy online) and Cheucle 2008 'Vers une description de la langue bekwel (A85b)' (Lyon 2 M2 mémoire, 214 pp., exists in Hammarström's private files only). searching relied on web lookups/curl against catalogues and APIs.

earlier_scan.source_named: Cheucle, Marion. 2014. Etude comparative des langues makaa-njem (bantu A80), Univ. Lyon 2 thesis, covers Bekwel phonology; not opened.

new_statements.quote: L'unité accentuelle, en bekwel, est le mot phonologique. Ce dernier correspond soit à une base nominale, soit à une base verbale. Il est généralement de structure -CVCVC et porte l'accent sur la syllabe initiale. En termes purement morphologiques, l'accent bekwel a pour domaine la syllabe initiale d'un thème nominal ou d'un thème verbal. [p. 338] ... En ce qui concerne le bekwel, l'argumentation développée jusqu'ici permet de dire qu'on a affaire à une langue à accent libre. [p. 339] ... le bekwel est une langue accentuelle; le domaine de l'accent est le thème nominal ou verbal. A l'intérieur de ce domaine, la proéminence est assignée à la position initiale, tandis que la syllabe est l'unité accentuable. [p. 209]
new_statements.translation: The accentual unit in Bekwel is the phonological word. The latter corresponds either to a nominal base or to a verbal base. It is generally of the structure -CVCVC and bears the accent on the initial syllable. In purely morphological terms, the Bekwel accent has as its domain the initial syllable of a nominal stem or of a verbal stem. [p. 338] ... As far as Bekwel is concerned, the argument developed so far allows us to say that we are dealing with a free-accent language. [p. 339] ... Bekwel is an accentual language; the domain of the accent is the nominal or verbal stem. Within this domain, prominence is assigned to the initial position, while the syllable is the accentuable unit. [p. 209]
new_statements.citation: Bouka, Léonce-Yembi. 1995. Structures phonologiques et structures prosodiques: le modèle bekwel. Thèse de doctorat, Université libre de Bruxelles, Faculté de Philosophie et Lettres. Chapitre V 'Accentologie et tonologie', §5.21.3 'Unité accentuable, unité accentuelle et domaine de l'accent'.
new_statements.locator: pp. 338-339 (vol. 2 scan, physical pp. 126-127); anticipatory statement p. 209 (vol. 1, ch. III); accent shifts §5.21.4 pp. 339-341; tone units §5.22.1 pp. 341-342
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Files opened: (172 physical pp.; extracted text of physical pp. 126-127 = thesis pp. 338-339, and the page-126 image inspected) and physical p. 222 = thesis p. 209, text + page image), plus the extract file. All three quoted passages are present verbatim at the stated locators: p. 338 "L'unité accentuelle, en bekwel, est le mot phonologique. Ce dernier correspond soit à une base nominale, soit à une base verbale. Il est généralement de structure -CVCVC et porte l'accent sur la syllabe initiale. En termes purement morphologiques, l'accent bekwel a pour domaine la syllabe initiale d'un thème nominal ou d'un thème verbal."; p. 339 "En ce qui concerne le bekwel, l'argumentation développée jusqu…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Accent falls on the first syllable of the noun or verb stem (thème); noun-class prefixes and other clitics are outside the accent domain, so the accented syllable is not counted from the word edge but from the stem — hence Bouka's 'accent libre' (morphologically, not phonologically, conditioned). The stem-initial syllable is labelled strong (s) and following syllables weak (w), building trochees (parametric conventions [184], p. 338-339). The 'accent' is a diacritic/metrical prominence argued from vowel length, a/0 alternation, resistance to glide reduction and tonal stability/attraction; its phonetic correlates were not measured. Bekwel is at the same time a tone language (tonemes H and B; surface H, B, lowered H, HB, BH).
new_statements.secondary_stress: No secondary stress posited for simple words. In compounds (determinative syntagms lexicalised as one word) Bouka identifies two prominence domains, one per nominal stem (p. 340). The Dominicy definition he quotes (p. 334) mentions secondary accent only in general terms.
new_statements.exceptions: Accent displacement (regressive or progressive) inside the clitic group: when a stem is reduced or deleted (e.g. -ân 'child' in mo-ân + connective + N), the accent shifts back onto the class prefix or forward onto the connective, dragging the stem's lexical tone with it — analysed as lexicalisation of prefix/connective into the stem (§5.21.4, pp. 339-341). Author notes the phonetic nature of the accent could not be investigated further (p. 331-332).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain = phonological word defined as the nominal or verbal stem (base), typically -CVCVC, excluding prefixes; a clitic-group level (prefix + stem, stem + connective) governs accent shift; phonological phrase relevant only marginally (conclusion p. 372-373). Data: elicited 1,200-entry lexicon and phrases from one reference informant (Christophe Lia), eastern (ebaa) dialect of Congo Bekwel.
new_statements.identity_note: Bouka 1995 describes the Bekwel of Congo-Brazzaville (Ouesso–Sembé–Souanké), specifically the eastern dialect 'ebaa' of his reference informant Christophe Lia (Intro §0.11); he distinguishes an eastern dialect (mekwoob, ebaa, zalagee) and a western one (mebeeza) in Congo, and notes Gabon Bekwel (Mekambo/Mvadi) = mebeeza and Cameroon Bekwel = esel. Cheucle 2014 (held, silent on stress) describes the Gabon variety (Ogooué-Ivindo). All fall under Glottolog bekw1242; no separate dialect glottocodes identified.

new_statements.quote: p. 159: « Dans mon lexique bekwel, je relève un fonctionnement tonal relativement simple, mais ceci est peut-être simplement dû au seul contexte étudié. On relève trois registres tonals : haut ([H]), bas ([B]) et moyen ([M]). » p. 160: « Pour les autres tons, je pose les schèmes /H/, /B/ et /HB/. » p. 161 (Tableau 17, Tons): « Registres [H], [B], [M] … Tonèmes /H/ et /B/ ; schèmes: /H/, /B/, /HB/, /BH/ ». p. 128: « … bloquée face à cette langue tonale … Les tons jouent un rôle au niveau lexical mais aussi grammatical. »
new_statements.translation: p. 159: 'In my Bekwel lexicon I find a relatively simple tonal system, but this may simply be due to the single context studied. Three tone registers are found: high ([H]), low ([B]) and mid ([M]).' p. 160: 'For the other tones I posit the patterns /H/, /B/ and /HB/.' p. 161 (Table 17, Tones): 'Registers [H], [B], [M] … Tonemes /H/ and /B/; patterns /H/, /B/, /HB/, /BH/.' p. 128: '… stuck in front of this tonal language … Tones play a role at the lexical and also the grammatical level.'
new_statements.citation: Cheucle, Marion (2014). Étude comparative des langues makaa-njem (bantu A80): phonologie, morphologie, lexique. Vers une reconstruction du proto-A80. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lumière Lyon 2 (dir. Lolke Van der Veen). Chapitre 3 'Données de première main' (Bekwel of Gabon, Ivindo), §2.5 Tons, pp. 159-161.
new_statements.locator: Thesis pp. 159 (§2.5.1 Inventaires des réalisations), 160 (§2.5.2 Fonction distinctive des tons) and 161 (§2.6 Récapitulatif, Tableau 17); also p. 128 (fieldwork narrative)
new_statements.reading: First-hand phonological sketch of Bekwel (Gabon) by a fieldworker: the language has lexical and grammatical tone with two tonemes /H/, /B/ (surface H, B, M, plus HB/BH contours). The whole recovered text (thesis pp. 1-169, which includes the complete Bekwel phonology sketch and its recapitulative table) contains no occurrence of 'accent', 'stress', 'prosod', 'intensité' or 'hauteur': the sketch is silent on word stress; no stress or accent is posited in the summary of 'the most salient traits of Bekwel phonology'. For a stress catalog this reads as 'tonal, no stress described' (silent-on-stress, not an explicit no-stress claim).
